To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the decoherence of labile protons in proteins, nucleic acids and polysaccharides is an intrinsic source of enhanced efficiency for homonuclear multidimentional NMR spectroscopy, and that these gains are particularly significant when the solvent exchange rates are fast.

the decoherence induced on labile protons through their solvent-exchange processes can, when suitfully manipulated, lead to sensitivity enhancements of ≈100–1000% for homonuclear multidimentional NMR experiments.

the decoherence of labile protons, which is a major limitation for the acquisition of homonuclear NMR experiments, can be exploited to enhance their sensitivity by orders of magnitude, when using Hadamard-encoded selective inversion or selective irradiation schemes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new family of experiments for NMR spectroscopy, which can be used to improve the sensitivity of homonuclear correlations for labile protons, such as those of water-exchangeable sites in proteins, oligosacchardes and nucleic acids.
the optimization of multidimensional NMR experiments for labile sites, and the resulting sensitivity gains can be used to enhance the efficiency of NMR experiments for the study of biomacromolecules.
the development of new methods for the enhancement of sensitivity and resolution in homonuclear multidimensionals.

the proposed methods provide a significant boost in the sensitivity of multidimensional TOCSY, NOESY, and other NMR experiments, particularly when applied to labile sites in macromolecules.

the present study provides an effective means for enhancing the sensitivity of NMR experiments that target labile sites in biomolecules, and that this approach is readily applicable to a wide range of systems, from proteins, nucleic acids and polysaccharides.

the proposed experiments can lead to significant enhancements in the sensitivity of homonuclear NMR correlations for sites with short lifetimes in proteins, polysccharides, and oligonucleotides.

the proposed methods provide a simple and efficient means for enhancing the sensitivity of NMR methods for labile sites, and thus should prove particularly useful in the analysis of protein, oligosacharide and nucleic acids.

, by exploiting the intrinsic properties of labile sites, the sensitivity of homonuclear TOCSY and/or NOESY can be significantly enhanced.
the sensitivity of NMR experiments can be significantly enhanced by manipulating the solvent exchange of labile protons.
the decoherence of labile protons in NMR can be exploited in the context of sensitivity enhancement, in experiments that are also considerably faster than conventional counterparts.
